newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra extends investment rules to uranium.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra extends investment rules to uranium.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday uranium mining would be subject to the same foreign investment rules as the rest of the mining industry.

Australia had no foreign investment policy for uranium mining before the new Liberal-National government won office in March and abolished the former Labor administration's limit on the industry to three particular mines.
Partly because of that limit, no foreigner ever applied to invest in uranium mines, even those that were allowed.
"The government has decided that the foreign investment policy in relation to the uranium sector will be the policy that currently applies to the mining sector generally," he said.

"The establishment of a new uranium mine involving investment of A$10 million or more, or the acquisition of a substantial interest in an existing uranium mining business valued at A$5 million or more, requires prior approval and no objections will be raised unless the proposal is considered contrary to the national interest," Costello said.
Any uranium mine applications would also have to include environmental proposals.
"There is also scope to impose conditions to protect the environment through foreign investment approvals," Costello said in a statement.
Export controls on uranium would continue to apply, he said.
